verdicts.reason: A rearranges the ad into a true left-to-right banner (phone, then headline and subline, then CTA) with a good two-line headline. It only needs polish: the CTA sits close to the right edge and the phone nearly touches the top and bottom. B just drops the original stacked layout into the middle of the wide canvas, leaving about 220px of dead space on each side, and its three-line headline wastes the width, so it reads as a pasted copy, not a banner.

A keeps the stacked copy column but strands it about 160px from the left edge, with a dead gap of about 260px before the phone at far right. The two halves feel disconnected, and the cramped three-line headline ignores the banner shape. B (the same as pair 1 A) is a proper horizontal layout with clear hierarchy and grouping; its only flaws are the tight right margin on the CTA and the phone almost touching the top and bottom edges.
